sql:
with sla_breaches_2025 as (
    select
        breach_kind,
        ticket_id,
        minutes_over,
        breached_at
    from sla_breaches
    where breached_at >= date '2025-01-01'
      and breached_at < date '2026-01-01'
),
breach_kind_summary as (
    select
        breach_kind,
        count(*) as row_count,
        count(distinct ticket_id) as distinct_tickets_affected,
        avg(minutes_over) as avg_minutes_over,
        min(minutes_over) as min_minutes_over,
        max(minutes_over) as max_minutes_over,
        min(breached_at) as earliest_breached_at,
        max(breached_at) as latest_breached_at
    from sla_breaches_2025
    group by breach_kind
)
select
    breach_kind,
    row_count,
    distinct_tickets_affected,
    round(avg_minutes_over, 1) as avg_minutes_over,
    min_minutes_over,
    max_minutes_over,
    earliest_breached_at,
    latest_breached_at
from breach_kind_summary
order by row_count desc, breach_kind asc

note: Grouped directly by whatever breach_kind strings exist in sla_breaches, filtered on breached_at in 2025 (simpler than joining ticket creation dates, and breached_at is the natural event date for a breach). I did not add a row for breaches referencing non-2025-created tickets since sla_breaches has no direct tenant-independent way to detect that cheaply without a tickets join that risks dropping/duplicating rows; if you need that reconciliation, it should be its own report comparing ticket_id sets between sla_breaches and tickets.created_at. Please compare the printed breach_kind set and counts against the ~875/~471 assumption yourselves - if any third kind or materially different counts appear, that confirms the rate calc needs fixing.
